scope: The Edinburgh weaver’s probable Duddingston father
publication_summary: This is a stronger local assessment of an existing father, not a new attachment, newly found source or live WikiTree save. The fixed pre-1850 working tree has 63 retained profiles below James and 972 on the other side of this edge; 61,236 connected pairs depend on it. These overlapping branch-impact counts measure priority, not a probability or 63 independently verified people. Working family membership and confidently marked connectivity are unchanged because probable remains below the confident grades. The prior effective uncertain flag, ungraded local assessment and plausible narrative are preserved. The printed 1641 apprenticeship page was re-read for this review; the burgess and burial citations use the maintained earlier source reviews, with the burial seen as an index rather than the original register. Robert Glasgow-1156 is now assessed as the probable father of James Glasgow-1150, the Edinburgh weaver. Grant’s 16 June 1641 apprenticeship names James’s father Robert and places the entry at Wester Duddingston with William Crichtoun and master William Sclaitter. The 20 June 1649 burgess admission repeats Sclaitter’s name and the exact apprenticeship date, securely connecting the recorded son to the adult weaver. The Robert buried at Duddingston on 17 January 1647 fits the father’s name, parish and preceding generation, six years after the apprenticeship and before James’s independent household began in 1649. Taken together, the specific local father and the Duddingston burial favour one Robert over an otherwise unattested second contemporary Robert in that parish. The previous assessment treated the lack of a unique identifier as a reason to stop at plausible; the combined argument warrants probable, while remaining an inference.
